issues.description: The supplied SAS entry point reads several unprovided DATA1 tables and writes its output to DATA1; the packaged CIK workbook is an identifier list, not a full analysis panel. Required DATA1/DATA librefs and compatible prepared-input routes are not defined in the source.

Author documentation describes EDGAR log conversion, government/IP filtering and index joining, but the Perl/SAS processing files and ARIN whois output mapping are absent; the immediate DATA1 event-panel producer cannot be traced.

The package lacks the author programs/schema needed to create the tax-footnote, 10-K length and similarity inputs. Local SEC and LM corpus roots exist, but only their root paths were checked; compatible filings, sections, years and cleaning were not verified.

The data description identifies the SAS file as the Tables 2–4 constructor and says Stata performs regression analysis; Tables 5–6 are separately described. The package contains no Stata program or separate Table 5–6 entry point, and the appendix lists additional tables/figures without a matching supplied analysis script.
DATA1 and DATA librefs are used by the supplied SAS program but not assigned there; no assigned library setup/autoexec is included in the package.

The code uses RSUBMIT, remote COMP.FUNDA and PROC DOWNLOAD without providing remote-session or library configuration. The current local Funda file is only a conditional candidate because required coverage and equivalence are not established.
The supplied SAS code invokes `%winsor` at the 1st and 99th percentiles, but its macro source/location is not included.
The supplied SAS code calls the FFINDL. format, but its format catalog/source is not included.

Two source expressions have unclear intended sample logic: the lagged CIK expression is compared with itself, and the code sets `drop="noncorp"` while a later filter checks `drop="notcorp"`. Do not infer replacements because either change can alter sample selection.

actions.description: Acquire only the documented public SEC source records after the author-selected periods and required files are confirmed.
steps: Use the official SEC older EDGAR log dataset for the target 2003–2015 years; follow current SEC fair-access guidance and retain its documented completeness limitations.
Obtain SEC full/quarterly index files for the same period to link accessions to filing form, CIK, date and file path.

Obtain author-required 10-K documents from the SEC archive after the author selection is confirmed; SEC archive history is public from 1994/1995 onward, while author-specific extraction remains separate.
validation: Confirm selected daily logs and index files cover the author-stated years and retain any SEC-reported gaps.
Check log fields against the official older-log variable list and index form/CIK/date/file mapping before any later authorized join.
Do not treat public annual IRS counts as event-level EDGAR logs or tax-text data.

actions.description: Request the prepared EDGAR tables or complete author-side producer contracts, and conditionally assess the author’s exact-study IRS Attention data request route without assuming it supplies the event-level panel.
steps: Request `data1.edgar_2003_2015_all` and `data1.firms_in_edgar_final`, or the exact SAS/Perl scripts, configuration and prepared ARIN/government-IP mapping that produce them.
Clarify the panel schema and population for CIK, accession, log date, filing type and government-download flags; identify the producer for the firm list described as firms downloaded by anyone.
Provide the DATA1 library assignment and any required autoexec/setup without exposing credentials in the package. SEC-published annual download totals are not a substitute for the event-level tables.

If the intended use is non-commercial and a prepared author dataset could address a missing input, consider the embedded author form, which requests name, workplace, and email; do not assume its delivery is event-level data or submit it during this assessment.

If any data are later received, inspect the files and schema and verify period, observation unit, fields, identifier keys, and joins before considering them compatible with data1.edgar_2003_2015_all or any other missing input.
validation: Use bounded metadata to confirm output fields and period; document how file type, CIK and download date join to the author firm list.
After separate execution authorization, compare the produced panel and firm list to the authors’ documented keys and sample counts.

Treat annual IRS-download counts as a distinct output unless the delivered data demonstrate the event-level CIK/accession/date/filing mapping required by the SAS panel; verify that this route does not substitute for tax-footnote or other workflow inputs.

actions.description: Clarify two sample-selection expressions before proposing any source change.
steps: Ask whether the lagged CIK condition was intended to compare the prior row CIK with the current row CIK; the supplied expression compares `lag(cik1)` with itself.
Ask whether the later `drop="notcorp"` test is intended to match the earlier `drop="noncorp"` values; do not silently change the category spelling.
Keep any source edit conditional until the author confirms intended sample rules and affected observations.
validation: After author clarification and separate execution authorization, compare row classifications, period coverage and sample counts with author-provided target outputs.

review_notes: Assessment is limited to the assigned package variant and its frozen source snapshot. Local SEC/LM probes checked only documented root existence, not contents or coverage.
No author code, regressions, downloads, installations, data extraction, patches or publishing were performed.

Its output unit, schema and delivery/coverage are unverified; the annual IRS-download counts are not treated as event-level EDGAR logs, prepared SAS panel inputs, tax-footnote data, or a full-analysis substitute.
